 The Internet Wants Kristen Stewart to Play a Bond Villain, and She Already Has the Look
 Her smoky eyes, wet-look hair and sharper recent cuts have a surprising amount in common with some of 007's most memorable foes.

 Robert Pattinson is the new James Bond , and the internet already has a role in mind for his former “Twilight” costar Kristen Stewart . And it’s not the Bond girl. Instead, fans want to see her with the skin of a killer as the villain opposite Pattinson in the next installment of the 007 franchise.
 The suggestion began making the rounds after Amazon MGM Studios announced Pattinson’s casting on Monday. It would reunite the former “Twilight” costars under rather different circumstances, and it seems like Stewart herself has been on board with the idea of playing a Bond villain for quite some time. In 2021, she told Daily Mail she would be interested in playing “the Bond girl who is the bad girl… who is the villain! I could play both parts”

 The Crossroads of Beauty 
 Before anyone gets too excited about the prospect of Stewart as a Bond villain or even a Bond girl, we have to note that there is currently no indication Stewart is joining the Denis Villeneuve -helmed film. But her recent hair and makeup style offer plenty of material for the fan campaign. Bond’s female antagonists have a history of memorable beauty looks, from Grace Jones’s sculptural hair as May Day to Famke Janssen’s dark-eyed glamour as Xenia Onatopp. Stewart has experimented with both, and a few things in between.
 Kristen Stewart at the “Nouvelles Vagues” International Biarritz Film Festival on June 27 in Biarritz, France. 
 Getty Images 
 At the Nouvelles Vagues Biarritz Film Festival in June, where she served as jury president, Stewart attended the closing ceremony with her short brunette hair plastered back, save for narrow, damp pieces curving over her forehead. 
 Charcoal shadow surrounded her eyes, including a heavy sweep beneath the lower lashes, while her lips remained almost bare. She paired the makeup with a Chanel tweed jacket over a black bra top.
 The hair brings to mind Jones in 1985’s “A View to a Kill,” even if Stewart’s wet, messy strands are different from May Day’s sharp, towering flat-top.
 Grace Jones in the 1985 James Bond Film “A View to a Kill.” 
 ©United Artists/Courtesy Everett Collection 
 Jones’s sculptural hairstyles — which sometimes featured a devilish curl at the front — and heavily defined eyes were as memorable as the character’s Alaïa wardrobe . But both Stewart and Jones’ May Day looks embrace a strong, masculine energy while still playing with softer, feminine details.
 Grace Jones in the 1985 James Bond Film “A View to a Kill.” 
 ©MGM/Courtesy Everett Collection 
 In May at Cannes, Stewart’s bixie went from a gelled, pushed-up style at the “Full Phil” photocall to neatly parted, face-framing bangs for the evening screening . There was another departure that night: bright red lipstick. Against her short brunette cut and red-and-black Chanel dress, the saturated lip was a rare bit of classic screen-siren makeup from an actress who generally favors a smoky eye.
 Kristen Stewart at the premiere for “Full Phil” at the 79th Festival de Cannes. 
 Michael Buckner 
 Janssen’s Xenia, introduced in 1995’s “GoldenEye,” had a particular fondness for brunette hair, dark liner and red lipstick. Stewart’s version came with a slightly undone finish. 
 Famke Janssen in the 1995 James Bond film, “GoldenEye.” 
 (c)United Artists/courtesy Everett Collection 
 For the Los Angeles premiere of “The Wrong Girls” in August, Stewart’s bixie transformed yet again, with separated bangs and wisps at the nape. Stewart paired it with warm brown shadow extending beyond the outer corners and worked beneath the lower lash line. A nude lip kept the eyes in focus.
 Kristen Stewart at “The Wrong Girls” Los Angeles premiere. 
 Jesse Grant 
 Stewart offered a different sort of Bond beauty back in November 2025. At the Governors Awards, Abergel swept her brunette hair into a high ponytail, exposing an undercut that wrapped around the sides of her head. Makeup artist Mai Quynh added pale mauve shadow extending toward her temples, with barely-there mascara.
 Kristen Stewart at the 16th Governors Awards on Nov. 16, 2025 in Los Angeles. 
 Jc Olivera 
 The somewhat slicked hair had something in common with Rosamund Pike’s controlled blond styling as double agent Miranda Frost in 2002’s “Die Another Day.” Frost, one suspects, would have kept the shaved sides a secret.
 Rosamund Pike in the 2002 James Bond film, “Die Another Day.” 
 ©MGM/Courtesy Everett Collection 
 While we are still presumably a ways away from knowing who will play a villain in the next installment of the James Bond franchise, here’s hoping that Villeneuve, who was just honored at the 2026 LACMA Art + Film Gala , keeps Stewart in mind.
